name: Google Analytics 4
summary: Google Analytics 4 is Google's free website and app analytics tool that tracks page views and custom events.

free_plan_covers.note: Standard GA4 properties are free with no published monthly cap on total events, only a limit of 100,000 events per user per day, far beyond what a small app would see.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Standard GA4 has no paid tier or monthly fee; the enterprise Google Analytics 360 upgrade has no published monthly price and is arranged directly with Google.

portability.note: You can export raw event data for free with BigQuery Export, up to 1 million events a day on standard properties, but GA4 itself is closed source with no self-hosting option.

cookies.note: GA4's standard setup sets first-party cookies like _ga to tell visitors apart and remember sessions across visits.

product_events.note: GA4 is built around events; besides automatic page views you can log recommended or fully custom events like sign_up or purchase.

setup.step: Create a Google Analytics 4 property and a web data stream, then copy its Measurement ID, which starts with G-.
Install the official integration with npm install @next/third-parties@latest next@latest.
Add the GoogleAnalytics component with your measurement ID to the root layout (app/layout.tsx).
Turn on Enhanced Measurement for the data stream so client-side route changes in Next.js count as page views.

builder_notes: Never send personal data such as names, emails or exact addresses as event parameters; Google Analytics' terms prohibit sending personally identifiable information.
GA4 sets cookies by default to identify visitors, so load it only after someone has consented to analytics cookies, or configure Google's Consent Mode.
